Performnace of this fused cute-dsl quantizer is better than cuda, a single API for dense and grouped mxfp8 linears, no need for scale rearrangements since swizzled layouts are directly output.

Consume TorchAO's landed fused dense rowwise/columnwise cast and single-axis
CuTeDSL casts directly, with blocked E8M0 scales and offs=None. Activation casts
live with weight quantization in tensor.py and use a shared RCEIL constant;
the existing square weight kernel's fixed RCEIL contract is explicitly enforced.
Select CuTeDSL automatically for 128-aligned BF16 operands, with no Linear/
converter backend option or saved autograd backend state. Use CUDA MXFP8 plus
blocked-scale rearrangement only for unsupported operand geometry, not missing
dependencies. Report missing AO/CuTeDSL dependencies with installation guidance
before that linear's parameter allocation. Preserve input-save formats,
32x32 RCEIL weight-scale policy, FSDP lifecycle, gradient destinations and
non-owned output behavior. Reject
unsupported required providers instead of padding or silently falling back.
Credit Protonu's #4895 kernel and Aleksandar's single-axis metadata work; only
landed AO #4995 is the runtime dependency.

Add complete PP2/VPP8/DP128 and PP4/VPP4/DP64, EP64 671B/MTP1 MLPerf recipes
using indexed aligned input sources, global strided ordering, GBS 15360/T4096
and fixed GBS 1024 validation. Reuse the earlier validation, MTP and dense-SDPA
interfaces. Include MXFP8 on the shared head, opt into its existing coalesced
training projection. Choose casts per actual operand: KV-A's aligned forward
input uses CuTeDSL, while its unsupported 576-wide output gradient uses CUDA.
The redundant recipe-level module-backend selector is removed.
Storage adapters and warmed checkpoint binding stay outside core TorchTitan.
Preserve current main's nested MLA KV-B projection selector, with an explicit
check that all 62 main/MTP projections retain MXFP8 rather than BF16 inputs.

Match NVIDIA's BF16 router GEMMs/logits/backward boundary, FP32 sigmoid and
selection, BF16 selected weights, unbiased top-8 sequence auxiliary coefficient
0.01, scale 2.5 and uncentered expert-bias update 0.001. Generic defaults remain
unchanged. Preserve FP32 persistent/final updates, BF16 gather/accumulation/
reduction/Adam moments, selective decay 0.033, clipping 1 and the zero-start
LR multipliers 0/.25/.5/.75/1 with a 11996-update cosine horizon.

Both optimizer/training and landed validation CUDA graphs are enabled.
Expose the existing graph wrapper's eager warmup count through TrainingConfig
(default2, production1) for both training and optimizer capture. Keep the
shared pool's landed eval-first readiness gate. Persisted map-dataset sharding
uses the explicit map_dataset_dp_sharding policy from the data PR. Forced
recipes select CF1; learned recipe defaults retain their conservative CF32 scratch
and minimum saved-activation policy. A run-specific wrapper may set measured
scratch/slot limits on the returned config. VMM and GraphTrainer are excluded.
Future router/sequence/CE fusion overrides are intentionally not imported at
this boundary; their integration belongs to the next three separate PRs.

## Verification

Owning-commit CPU checks: 152 passed, 19 warnings in 34.43s.

Strict relevant Sphinx builds and all non-type repository hooks passed.
Three unchanged main type findings remain attributed, not reported as a clean
full type run. External reviewer and CI acceptance are separate, still pending.

Complete-stack integration (not this PR in isolation): real four-GPU PP2/DP2/
EP2 and PP4/DP1/EP1 ran ten updates with exact model/optimizer tensor parity,
optimizer graphs and sequential validation. A fresh native PP2/PP4 checkpoint
matrix matched resumed state exactly. These are debug-model contract checks,
not 671B throughput or convergence results.

The final 207-case GPU matrix covers in-place gradients, dense attention, PP/FSDP train/eval graphs, shared-stream backward/capture and fused numerical contracts.

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 4m 13s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41279136773) --- **Verdict: changes requested.** The MXFP8 part addresses @anijain2305's three comments. The main issue is that the PR also bundles about six independent core behavior changes under an MXFP8 title, and one new config field only partly takes effect in GraphTrainer. (The `/pr-review` skill isn't installed in this environment, so this review is posted as this comment rather than as a GitHub review with inline comments.) ### Blocking **1. Split this PR. The title and scope don't match.** Besides the activation-cast change, it changes shared core code that every model uses: - `LRSchedulersContainer.Config.warmup_start_factor` (`components/optim/lr_scheduler.py:82`) - `TrainingConfig.cuda_graph_warmup_steps`, threaded through `Optim` and `TrainingEngine` - `Sigmoid.Config.compute_dtype` (`models/common/activation.py`) - `TokenChoiceTopKRouter.Config.routing_weight_dtype`, and the router `gate` type widened from `HiMidLoLinear.Config` to `Linear.Config` (`models/common/moe/moe.py:184`) - `MoE.Config.center_expert_bias_update`, plus a new `_MoELike` protocol member (`moe.py:757`) - a new `MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss._compute_local_stats` override hook (`moe.py:572`) - four 671B MLPerf recipes, `overrides/dsv3_mlperf.py`, and about 100 lines of MTP docs Each of these needs its own justification and numerics evidence under the root CLAUDE.md rules ("Protect battle-tested code paths", "Show numerical proof"). A reviewer can't approve the MXFP8 kernel switch without also signing off on router precision and LR-schedule semantics. Suggested split: - (a) MXFP8 CuTeDSL activation casts: `tensor.py`, `linear.py`, the README and the MXFP8 tests - (b) the scheduler and CUDA-graph warmup knobs - (c) the router and MoE precision and bias-update knobs - (d) the MLPerf recipes, stacked on (a)–(c) **2. `cuda_graph_warmup_steps` only partly applies in GraphTrainer.** `GraphTrainingEngine` inherits the optimizer construction, so the optimizer graph uses the new config value. Its fwd/bwd wrapper still hard-codes the constant at `torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/trainer.py:204` (`num_warmup_iterations=NUM_CUDA_GRAPH_WARMUP_STEPS`). With `cuda_graph_warmup_steps=1`, the optimizer would capture after one call and fwd/bwd after two, with no warning. - Either read the config value there too, or reject or warn for values other than 2 under GraphTrainer. - Also, `Optim.__init__` still defaults to `NUM_CUDA_GRAPH_WARMUP_STEPS` while `TrainingConfig` hard-codes `2`. That is two sources of truth for the same default. Consider making the `Optim` parameter required, since `TrainingEngine` always passes it. **3. CPU tests may now fail when constructing `MXFP8Linear`.** `MXFP8Linear.__init__` now calls `_require_cutedsl_activation_quantizers()` (`quantization/mxfp8/linear.py:362`). That raises unless `quant._mxfp8_cutedsl_kernels_available` is true, and its error message ties that to SM10.x plus the CuTeDSL runtime. - The existing CPU test `test_mxfp8_linear_loads_stock_checkpoint` (`tests/unit_tests/cpu/quantization/test_quantization.py:949`) builds an `MXFP8Linear` on CPU. On a runner without the CuTe runtime it will now hit the `ImportError`. - CPU Unit Test was **skipped** in CI because this is a stacked PR, and the "152 passed" in the description doesn't say what hardware it ran on. Please confirm it passes on a GPU-less runner. - The new CPU tests import `torchao.prototype.moe_training...` without an `importorskip` guard. ### Non-blocking
MXFP8 cast path (tensor.py) - **Scale shape differs by path.** The CuTe path returns 1-D `flatten()`ed scales, while the CUDA fallback returns the 2-D output of `triton_mx_block_rearrange`. `scaled_mm` apparently accepts both, and your end-to-end backward test covers it. Please say in the docstring that scale shape is path-dependent, or flatten both, so a later consumer doesn't rely on one shape. - **Repeated dependency check.** `_require_cutedsl_activation_quantizers()` runs `inspect.signature` and the import probes once per `MXFP8Linear` instance, which is hundreds of times for 671B. It's cheap, but `functools.cache` makes it run once. - **Axis naming.** `tensor.py` line 130 transposes the fused kernel's columnwise output (`col.t()`), but the single-axis 32x1 path at line 149 returns `col` as is. Presumably AO returns different layouts for the two. A one-line comment would make clear this is intended. The bitwise tests compare `.contiguous().flatten()`, which checks values, not strides. - **Old TODO concerns.** The removed TODO's concerns are now addressed: 32-row vs 128-row alignment through the per-operand CUDA fallback, and dependency gating at construction. Good.
Router, MoE and LR scheduler - **Why disable `inplace_wgrad_accum` on the MLPerf gate?** `_mlperf_dsv3_model_policy` (`torchtitan_recipes/models/deepseek_v3.py:86`) sets it to `False` for the rebuilt gate without explaining why. Please add a one-line reason. - **Redundant normalization.** `_unbiased_routing_map` (`overrides/dsv3_mlperf.py:20`) divides by a positive per-row constant before `topk`. That doesn't change the selection, so the division can be dropped. `_compute_local_stats` then recomputes the same normalization. - **`warmup_start_factor` semantics.** With `0.0`, the first optimizer step runs at lr=0 but still updates the AdamW moments. That is intended for MLPerf; the docstring could say so explicitly.
Recipe questions - `steps=60` (`deepseek_v3.py:235`) against `total_steps=11996`: is the 60 a placeholder for local runs? A recipe named `_mlperf` that stops at step 60 is surprising. - `Validator.Config(freq=1, steps=1)` (`deepseek_v3.py:202`) runs validation after every training step. Is that the intended MLPerf cadence? - Typos with missing spaces in `MTP.md`: "explicit16-stage", "sequence4096", "trainGBS15360", "uses256", "top-k8", "scale2.5", "emits576", "its576-wide".
CI The latest B200 Integration run (10-23) failed 2 tests: `kimi_k3_fsdp2_tp2_ep2_pp2_vpp4` and `dist_moe_eager_fsdp_ep_pp_cudagraph`. Both fail with `ValueError: Unexpected keyword arguments with pre-split inputs: loss_results`. That is a PP schedule kwarg problem, most likely from the base PR (`dsv3-mtp-loss-metrics`) rather than this change. The `mxfp8_linear_fsdp` integration test passed.
Consider moving this to torchtitan/quantization/mxfp8/tensor.py where we already have a quantize method

+"""Unbiased sequence balancing used by the DeepSeek-V3 MLPerf recipes."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+from torchtitan.models.common.moe import MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss
+
+__all__ = ["UnbiasedTopKLoadBalanceLoss"]
+
+# T = tokens, E = experts, K = experts selected per token.
+
+
+def _unbiased_routing_map(scores_TE, top_k, *, padding_mask_T=None):
+    """Select plain top-k after NVIDIA's unbiased positive-score normalization."""
+    normalized_TE = scores_TE / (scores_TE.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-20)
+    expert_ids_TK = normalized_TE.topk(top_k, dim=-1, sorted=False).indices
+    routing_map_TE = torch.zeros_like(scores_TE, dtype=torch.bool).scatter_(
+        -1, expert_ids_TK, True
+    )
+    return (
+        routing_map_TE
+        if padding_mask_T is None
+        else routing_map_TE & ~padding_mask_T.unsqueeze(-1)
+    )
+
+
+class UnbiasedTopKLoadBalanceLoss(MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss):
+    """Compute sequence balancing from scores, not dispatch bias or forced routes."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss.Config):
+        top_k: int
+        """Number of unbiased expert choices counted per valid token."""
+
+        def __post_init__(self):
+            if self.top_k <= 0:
+                raise ValueError("top_k must be positive")
+
+    def __init__(self, config: Config):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        self.top_k = config.top_k
+
+    def _compute_local_stats(self, scores_TE, routing_map_TE, padding_mask_T):
+        """Use NVIDIA's positive-score denominator, including tiny sigmoid rows."""
+        counts_E = routing_map_TE.to(scores_TE.dtype).sum(0)
+        normalized_TE = scores_TE / (scores_TE.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-20)
+        if padding_mask_T is not None:
+            normalized_TE = normalized_TE * ~padding_mask_T.unsqueeze(-1)
+        return counts_E, normalized_TE.sum(0)
+
+    def forward(
+        self, scores_TE, routing_map_TE, *, carrier, padding_mask_T=None, denominator
+    ):
+        """Reuse upstream normalization/injection with the independent top-k map."""
+        del routing_map_TE
+        unbiased_map_TE = _unbiased_routing_map(
+            scores_TE, self.top_k, padding_mask_T=padding_mask_T
+        )
+        return super().forward(
+            scores_TE,
+            unbiased_map_TE,
+            carrier=carrier,
+            padding_mask_T=padding_mask_T,
+            denominator=denominator,
+        )

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 4m 13s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41279136773) --- **Verdict: changes requested.** The MXFP8 part addresses @anijain2305's three comments. The main issue is that the PR also bundles about six independent core behavior changes under an MXFP8 title, and one new config field only partly takes effect in GraphTrainer. (The `/pr-review` skill isn't installed in this environment, so this review is posted as this comment rather than as a GitHub review with inline comments.) ### Blocking **1. Split this PR. The title and scope don't match.** Besides the activation-cast change, it changes shared core code that every model uses: - `LRSchedulersContainer.Config.warmup_start_factor` (`components/optim/lr_scheduler.py:82`) - `TrainingConfig.cuda_graph_warmup_steps`, threaded through `Optim` and `TrainingEngine` - `Sigmoid.Config.compute_dtype` (`models/common/activation.py`) - `TokenChoiceTopKRouter.Config.routing_weight_dtype`, and the router `gate` type widened from `HiMidLoLinear.Config` to `Linear.Config` (`models/common/moe/moe.py:184`) - `MoE.Config.center_expert_bias_update`, plus a new `_MoELike` protocol member (`moe.py:757`) - a new `MicrobatchWiseLoadBalanceLoss._compute_local_stats` override hook (`moe.py:572`) - four 671B MLPerf recipes, `overrides/dsv3_mlperf.py`, and about 100 lines of MTP docs Each of these needs its own justification and numerics evidence under the root CLAUDE.md rules ("Protect battle-tested code paths", "Show numerical proof"). A reviewer can't approve the MXFP8 kernel switch without also signing off on router precision and LR-schedule semantics. Suggested split: - (a) MXFP8 CuTeDSL activation casts: `tensor.py`, `linear.py`, the README and the MXFP8 tests - (b) the scheduler and CUDA-graph warmup knobs - (c) the router and MoE precision and bias-update knobs - (d) the MLPerf recipes, stacked on (a)–(c) **2. `cuda_graph_warmup_steps` only partly applies in GraphTrainer.** `GraphTrainingEngine` inherits the optimizer construction, so the optimizer graph uses the new config value. Its fwd/bwd wrapper still hard-codes the constant at `torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/trainer.py:204` (`num_warmup_iterations=NUM_CUDA_GRAPH_WARMUP_STEPS`). With `cuda_graph_warmup_steps=1`, the optimizer would capture after one call and fwd/bwd after two, with no warning. - Either read the config value there too, or reject or warn for values other than 2 under GraphTrainer. - Also, `Optim.__init__` still defaults to `NUM_CUDA_GRAPH_WARMUP_STEPS` while `TrainingConfig` hard-codes `2`. That is two sources of truth for the same default. Consider making the `Optim` parameter required, since `TrainingEngine` always passes it. **3. CPU tests may now fail when constructing `MXFP8Linear`.** `MXFP8Linear.__init__` now calls `_require_cutedsl_activation_quantizers()` (`quantization/mxfp8/linear.py:362`). That raises unless `quant._mxfp8_cutedsl_kernels_available` is true, and its error message ties that to SM10.x plus the CuTeDSL runtime. - The existing CPU test `test_mxfp8_linear_loads_stock_checkpoint` (`tests/unit_tests/cpu/quantization/test_quantization.py:949`) builds an `MXFP8Linear` on CPU. On a runner without the CuTe runtime it will now hit the `ImportError`. - CPU Unit Test was **skipped** in CI because this is a stacked PR, and the "152 passed" in the description doesn't say what hardware it ran on. Please confirm it passes on a GPU-less runner. - The new CPU tests import `torchao.prototype.moe_training...` without an `importorskip` guard. ### Non-blocking
MXFP8 cast path (tensor.py) - **Scale shape differs by path.** The CuTe path returns 1-D `flatten()`ed scales, while the CUDA fallback returns the 2-D output of `triton_mx_block_rearrange`. `scaled_mm` apparently accepts both, and your end-to-end backward test covers it. Please say in the docstring that scale shape is path-dependent, or flatten both, so a later consumer doesn't rely on one shape. - **Repeated dependency check.** `_require_cutedsl_activation_quantizers()` runs `inspect.signature` and the import probes once per `MXFP8Linear` instance, which is hundreds of times for 671B. It's cheap, but `functools.cache` makes it run once. - **Axis naming.** `tensor.py` line 130 transposes the fused kernel's columnwise output (`col.t()`), but the single-axis 32x1 path at line 149 returns `col` as is. Presumably AO returns different layouts for the two. A one-line comment would make clear this is intended. The bitwise tests compare `.contiguous().flatten()`, which checks values, not strides. - **Old TODO concerns.** The removed TODO's concerns are now addressed: 32-row vs 128-row alignment through the per-operand CUDA fallback, and dependency gating at construction. Good.
Router, MoE and LR scheduler - **Why disable `inplace_wgrad_accum` on the MLPerf gate?** `_mlperf_dsv3_model_policy` (`torchtitan_recipes/models/deepseek_v3.py:86`) sets it to `False` for the rebuilt gate without explaining why. Please add a one-line reason. - **Redundant normalization.** `_unbiased_routing_map` (`overrides/dsv3_mlperf.py:20`) divides by a positive per-row constant before `topk`. That doesn't change the selection, so the division can be dropped. `_compute_local_stats` then recomputes the same normalization. - **`warmup_start_factor` semantics.** With `0.0`, the first optimizer step runs at lr=0 but still updates the AdamW moments. That is intended for MLPerf; the docstring could say so explicitly.
Recipe questions - `steps=60` (`deepseek_v3.py:235`) against `total_steps=11996`: is the 60 a placeholder for local runs? A recipe named `_mlperf` that stops at step 60 is surprising. - `Validator.Config(freq=1, steps=1)` (`deepseek_v3.py:202`) runs validation after every training step. Is that the intended MLPerf cadence? - Typos with missing spaces in `MTP.md`: "explicit16-stage", "sequence4096", "trainGBS15360", "uses256", "top-k8", "scale2.5", "emits576", "its576-wide".
